key_correction.kind: incorrect source/key fact; no new question
key_correction.actual_request: When you use your own Energy Charge, how much Ammo may it restore and to what type of Weapon? What alternative Door effect can you choose, and which Doors are in range?
key_correction.incorrect_key_clause: The Item is Out of Combat Only
key_correction.source_finding: The complete English Energy Charge card in the middle-column component illustration on printed page 23 has no Combat restriction icon. The adjacent Clothes and Bandages cards visibly have the crossed-guns icon; Energy Charge does not. Under the explicit unmarked-card rule (page 12), Energy Charge is usable in Combat as well as outside it, subject to its own targets/payment. Compatible PL/FR/DE page-23 cards show the same absence. The author map's Q117 purported primary passage incorrectly inserts an Out of Combat Only tag.

sources.location: Component Item illustrations: complete Energy Charge card
In Combat Only / Out of Combat Only

sources.paraphrase: Compatible full card also lacks a Combat restriction icon.
Compatible full card also lacks a Combat restriction icon.
Compatible full card also lacks a Combat restriction icon.

key_correction.corrected_expected_answer: Either fully load one of your own Energy Weapons (up to its capacity), OR Open or Close 1 Door in a Corridor connected to your current Room. The Door alternative does not also reload a Weapon. The Item has no Combat restriction icon, so it may be used in or out of Combat subject to its own requirements. It costs 1 Action card and is One Use Only. The ordinary prohibition on closing Destroyed Doors still applies; Energy Charge is not the Plasma Torch exception.
required_changes: Remove the false Out of Combat Only assertion from Q117 key.
Correct the author coverage map's Q117 primary-passage transcription.
Do not allocate a new ID for applying the already-requested unmarked-card rule (Q55/Q82) to this Item.
key_correction.request_scope_note: Combat legality was additional context in this key, not an extra requirement to impose on a reader answering the narrower Q117 request. It must nevertheless not contradict the raw source.

accepted_additions.topic: Suppression escape spends Ammo, moves one consenting selected Character, and suppresses Escape attacks
accepted_additions.question: The Captain plays Suppressive Fire, whose printed Action cost is 0. Must any Ammo still be spent? Does it move both the Captain and another Character, or one selected Character; must that other Character agree, and are the normal Escape attacks resolved?
accepted_additions.expected_answer: Discard 1 Ammo as the card instructs. Move either yourself OR 1 other chosen Character in your Room, with that Character's agreement. It does not move both. This movement does not trigger an Intruder Attack. The printed 0 does not waive the separate Ammo requirement; the played Action card itself is still discarded under the ordinary card-play rule.

sources.location: Actions from Action cards illustration: Captain Suppressive Fire (rightmost card)
sources.paraphrase: The card shows cost 0 and In Combat Only, then an Ammo discard, a self-or-one-other agreed movement, and an explicit waiver of Intruder Attack.
Normal Escape causes attacks; the prose expressly identifies Suppressive Fire as a card that modifies Escape.
Compatible card wording corroborates the Ammo payment, choosing self or another willing Character, and movement without an Intruder Attack.
Compatible illustration corroborates one Ammo and escape without an Intruder Attack.

closest_requests.actual_request: A Character Escapes a Room with two Intruders toward an empty unexplored Room. When do attacks occur, who is targeted, what happens if they die, and what follows if they survive?

Can Soldier use Covering Fire only on themselves, and how are direction, Noise and Surprise targeting handled when moving two Characters?
May Captain use Order while personally in Combat; may Intercom force someone else to Move out of Combat and what rules apply?

accepted_additions.novelty_reason: Q14 and Q65 ask the ordinary Escape attacks and order; Q82 asks which action families are legal in Combat; Q83 asks Soldier Covering Fire's two-Character direction/Noise/Surprise handling; Q87 asks Captain Order/Intercom and expressly applies normal Escape. None requests Suppressive Fire's separate Ammo payment, self-OR-other selection, consent, or attack waiver. This is a different movement outcome and resource requirement, not merely a new Character name or a recombination of ordinary Escape.
accepted_additions.why_not_existing_key_repair: Adding these card-specific requirements to Q14/Q83/Q87 would require facts those actual requests do not ask.

accepted_additions.topic: Nemesis Plans checks two unexplored Room tiles but forbids inspecting their Exploration tokens
accepted_additions.question: When you use Nemesis Plans, how many unexplored Room tiles may you check, may you also inspect their Exploration tokens as with Monitoring Room, and what are the Item's Action-card cost and use restrictions?
accepted_additions.expected_answer: Check any 2 unexplored Room tiles, but do not look at their Exploration tokens. Pay 1 Action card; the Item is One Use Only and Out of Combat Only, so discard it after use. Monitoring Room instead checks 1 unexplored Room tile together with its Exploration token.

sources.location: Actions from Item cards illustration: Nemesis Plans (rightmost card)
sources.paraphrase: The English illustration explicitly says two unexplored Room tiles and excludes their Exploration tokens; cost 1, One Use Only and crossed-guns icon are visible.
The Room action includes one unexplored Room and its Exploration token.
Compatible card illustration corroborates two Room tiles and explicitly excludes Exploration tokens.
Compatible illustration independently corroborates the same two-tile, no-Exploration-token distinction.

accepted_additions.topic: Scientist's Pistol overrides the ordinary two-crosshair Shoot result
accepted_additions.question: With no Weakness modifying damage, you Shoot an Intruder using the Scientist's Pistol and roll the two-crosshair result. How many Injuries do you place, and do you still check the Injury Effect?
accepted_additions.expected_answer: Only 1 Injury, because the Scientist's Pistol treats a two-hit roll as one hit. Then resolve the ordinary Injury Effect check for the Intruder. The example on printed page 19 places one Injury on an Adult and draws one Attack card for the blood comparison.

sources.location: Combat Example, left column and illustrated Pistol
sources.paraphrase: The English prose explicitly overrides two hits to one for the Scientist's Pistol, places one Injury, then checks endurance using an Intruder Attack card.
Ordinary two-crosshair Shooting gives two Injuries, with Weapon special rules capable of modifying it.

accepted_additions.novelty_reason: The closest actual request Q12 expressly asks an ordinary Shoot-versus-Melee comparison. Its key correctly says ordinary two-hit Shooting gives 2, subject to Weapon text; neither the request nor key names the Scientist's Pistol or supplies its mapping of two hits to one. Q52 asks species eligibility, Q70 a Fire Weakness bonus, Q103 starting Ammo, Q115 Flamethrower minimum damage/Fire, and Q120 Six Shooter's single-crosshair bonus. No request asks this inverse damage exception. The author's rejection labels it an example of an existing rule, but the example contains a concrete Weapon exception that cannot be recovered from the generic statement that exceptions exist.
accepted_additions.why_not_existing_key_repair: Q12 is not wrong. Making its ordinary-action answer require this named Weapon would impose unasked detail. A new explicit exception request is the clean repair.

request_scope: Source-backed key context does not become a requirement when unasked by a stem.
